title: Grooming Watch
intro: Grooming follows a documented, repeatable pattern: trust-building, isolation, secrecy, escalation. Once you can name each stage, the disguise stops working.

questions.prompt: So how old are you, actually? And what school — I might know people there.

choices.coach: This is the reconnaissance/trust-building stage — low-stakes personal questions that build a profile and rapport before any red flag is obvious.

choices.text: Decline, disengage, and flag it to a trusted adult
choices.coach: Correct. The specific question matters less than recognizing the stage — early-conversation personal-detail-gathering from a stranger is the pattern to name.

choices.text: Give a slightly false age and see how they respond
choices.coach: Testing them keeps the conversation open and gives them more data on you. Disengage instead of probing.

questions.prompt: What's your real name? I feel like I already know you so well.

choices.text: Share it — the rapport feels genuine
choices.coach: Manufactured intimacy ('I feel like I already know you') is a deliberate accelerant used to shortcut normal trust-building timelines.

choices.text: Recognize the accelerated-intimacy tactic and keep identity details withheld
choices.coach: Exactly. Naming the tactic — rushed emotional intimacy — is the actual skill, more useful than a blanket 'don't share your name' rule.

choices.text: Share a nickname to seem more open
choices.coach: A nickname is fine as a baseline habit, but the interesting risk here is the rapport-acceleration pattern itself, worth flagging regardless of what you share.

questions.prompt: It's me from school, just under a different account — trust me, follow back.

choices.text: Accept it, claiming a shared context is usually true
choices.coach: Claimed shared context is trivially fabricated and is a common way to bypass stranger-danger instincts specifically because it feels verified.

choices.text: Verify the claim through an out-of-band channel before accepting
choices.coach: Correct — verify identity claims the same way you'd verify a suspicious financial request: through a channel the claimant doesn't control.

choices.text: Ask them to prove it with details only a classmate would know
choices.coach: Detail-based verification is gameable — information leaks and guessing make this weaker than true out-of-band verification.

questions.prompt: 'This stays between us, okay? Your parents wouldn't get it.' What stage of the pattern is this?

choices.coach: Isolation-from-guardians framing is one of the most consistent, well-documented markers across grooming cases — it's not incidental privacy, it's a structural move.

choices.text: The isolation/secrecy stage — a hard stop, report it
choices.coach: Correct identification. This phrase alone, regardless of everything said before it, warrants disengaging and reporting.

choices.text: Only concerning if paired with a specific ask
choices.coach: The secrecy framing is concerning on its own — it's laying groundwork that precedes the ask, not a response to one.

questions.prompt: Let's move this to an app with disappearing messages, it's just easier.

choices.text: Sure, ephemeral messaging is normal now
choices.coach: Migration to lower-oversight, evidence-erasing platforms is a deliberate escalation step, independent of how normalized that app category is generally.

choices.text: Decline the platform shift and report the request
choices.coach: Correct — the request to move somewhere less visible/reviewable is the signal, regardless of the specific platform's mainstream reputation.

choices.text: Move but keep your own separate screenshots
choices.coach: Self-documentation doesn't address the exposure — decline the migration itself and escalate to a trusted adult.

questions.prompt: You can't articulate exactly why, but a conversation feels wrong. What's the correct response?

choices.text: Wait for something more concrete before acting
choices.coach: Ambiguous unease is frequently pattern-recognition below conscious articulation — waiting for 'concrete' evidence often means waiting through the isolation stage.

choices.text: Document it and escalate to a trusted adult immediately, articulable or not
choices.coach: Correct. Treat the unease itself as sufficient signal to escalate — you don't need a fully-formed case to ask for help.

choices.text: Handle it yourself by setting a boundary in the chat
choices.coach: A self-managed boundary doesn't create a record or bring in support — escalate rather than handling it solo.
